text:
Maria Vega: Quick sync — proposing a 'graduated-safety' fallback approach for A/B/canary rollouts: score-based decision surface with hysteresis. Primary goal: prefer low-latency variant unless quality regressions exceed threshold, then fallback to cached or older model. Thoughts?
Jonah Patel: how do we compute score? latency vs quality weights?
Maria Vega: thinking of composite score = w1*(normalized_p95_latency) + w2*(1 - normalized_quality) + penalty_for_errors. Lower score wins. For heat-up canary we bias towards stability.
Alex R.: session affinity concern — if we cut traffic mid-session we can confuse clients. Can we do soft-eviction: route existing sessions to original variant until session end + short grace?
Cheng Li: telemetry hooks needed. We should expose per-variant: p50/p95, error-rate, eval-regressions, cache-hit-rate. Also expose a 'fallback-risk' gauge.
Sara N: +1. Add an automated canary warmup: ramp 0->X over N minutes and only start score evaluation after warmup completes.
Jonah Patel: what about hysteresis thresholds to prevent flip-flopping? e.g. must exceed threshold for T consecutive windows or delta > D for M minutes.
Maria Vega: exactly. Proposed params:
```
{ "warmup_minutes": 5, "consecutive_windows": 3, "window_size_sec": 60, "hysteresis_delta": 0.08 }
```
Alex R.: sticky sessions + soft-eviction pseudo-config:
```
{ "respect_affinity": true, "grace_period_sec": 300, "drain_mode": "best-effort" }
```
Cheng Li: operator controls: manual override, automatic rollback triggers (high-error, QoL regression, SLO breach), and an experimental dry-run mode that logs decisions but doesn't route.
Sara N: Eval integration: tie quality signal to pre-defined prompt set. If regression > 1% on N prompts then penalize heavily.
Jonah Patel: Do we need a separate 'fallback-orchestrator' service or can this live in router? Tradeoffs?
Maria Vega: prefer a small dedicated orchestrator (stateless control plane) that publishes decision snapshots to routers. Routers remain simple enforcers; orchestrator handles scoring, history, audits, and rollbacks.
Alex R.: makes sense for audit trails. Also need a negotiation protocol for multi-router consensus (TTL based snapshots + versioned decisions).
Cheng Li: add a probe design: lightweight synthetic requests to shadow variant every window to measure perf/err. Include sampling config.
Jonah Patel: sample probe payloads should be small and representative. Avoid heavy tokens.
Maria Vega: draft rollout policy snippet (for console/infra):
```
{"policy_name": "grad-safety-v1",
 "routing_preference": "latency_first",
 "thresholds": {"quality": 0.98, "error_rate": 0.01},
 "fallback_action": "route_to_stable",
 "monitoring": ["p95_latency","eval_regression","error_rate"]
}
```
Sara N: ops playbook: on fallback trigger - notify #eng-oncall, mute canary alerts for 5m if operator is investigating, fallback snap stored for rollback. @deploy-bot make sure we record the exact decision payload.
deploy-bot: Rollout plan recorded: id=rb-20240301-22, snapshot_url=https://console.redwood/reports/rb-20240301-22 :white_check_mark:
Maria Vega: next steps: I'll write RFC with scoring math, required metrics, APIs for orchestrator->router snapshot, and canary warmup knobs. Assigning owners: @Cheng for telemetry, @Alex for session-affinity/drain, @Sara for playbook. Ping me if you want to pair on sections.
Jonah Patel: Thanks — happy to help on scoring tests.
Cheng Li: I'll add the probe implementation prototype to eng-runtime branch and open PR.
Alex R.: I'll prototype session drain semantics in the router shim.
Sara N: I'll draft the ops runbook and alerts.
Maria Vega: Great. Meeting to sync on RFC Friday 10am? :calendar:
Jonah Patel: works for me :+1:
Cheng Li: works
Alex R.: ok
Sara N: +1
